title: Hospital Value-Based Programs: VBP, HRRP, and HACRP
summary: CMS runs three major value-based programs for hospitals under traditional Medicare: the Hospital Value-Based Purchasing Program (VBP), the Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program (HRRP), and the Hospital-Acquired Condition Reduction Program (HACRP). Together, they tie approximately 6% of DRG payments to quality performance.

objectives.text: Describe how the Hospital VBP Program adjusts DRG payments based on quality
Explain the conditions targeted by HRRP and the magnitude of potential penalties
Identify the hospital-acquired conditions measured by HACRP

content_blocks.body: The Affordable Care Act of 2010 introduced three mandatory value-based purchasing programs for hospitals that participate in Medicare — creating financial consequences for quality performance rather than simply paying for volume.

VBP withholds 2% of all DRG payments and redistributes them based on hospital quality scores across four domains:

1. **Clinical outcomes** — mortality rates for AMI, HF, pneumonia, COPD, CABG; PSI-90 (patient safety composite)
2. **Safety** — healthcare-associated infections (CLABSI, CAUTI, MRSA, CDI)
3. **Person and Community Engagement** — HCAHPS patient experience survey scores
4. **Efficiency and Cost Reduction** — Medicare spending per beneficiary

Hospitals that score above average receive bonuses; those below average receive net reductions. Budget-neutral design means total dollars redistributed equal total dollars withheld.

HRRP penalizes hospitals with excess 30-day readmission rates for six conditions: **AMI, HF, pneumonia, COPD, hip/knee replacement, and CABG.** Maximum penalty is 3% of all Medicare DRG payments — a significant financial exposure for high-readmission hospitals.

HRRP has been controversial. Critics argue it has worsened patient outcomes in some cases (patients diverted from admission when they needed hospitalization) and disproportionately penalizes safety-net hospitals that serve higher-risk, sicker populations. A 2022 adjustment stratifies hospitals by the proportion of dual-eligible patients they serve, partially addressing the equity critique.

HACRP imposes a **1% payment reduction** on the lowest-performing quartile of hospitals for hospital-acquired conditions, including:

- Central line-associated bloodstream infections (CLABSI)
- Catheter-associated urinary tract infections (CAUTI)
- Surgical site infections (SSI)
- Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) bacteremia
- Clostridium difficile infections (CDI)
- Patient Safety Indicator composite (PSI-90)

Unlike VBP (which sets absolute and improvement thresholds), HACRP always penalizes the bottom 25% regardless of absolute performance — creating persistent pressure even as overall rates improve.
